p1511.title: feat(cli): spawn-peer CLI + MCP spawn_peer for peer spawn with remit

nodes.body:
**Findings**
- [Minor] Validate the required CLI name before spawning — `--name` only rejects blank input, while the hub rename schema caps names at 255 characters and `spawnPeer` deliberately continues after a rename failure. A 256-character title therefore creates and messages a peer, then exits 0 under a different name, so callers cannot rely on the required title. Evidence `cli/src/commands/spawnPeer.ts:247` (failure handling context: `cli/src/modules/spawnPeer/spawnPeer.ts:301`).
  Suggested fix:
  ```ts
  const name = parsed.name?.trim() ?? ''
  if (!name || name.length > 255) {
      throw new SpawnPeerError('bad_args', '--name must be 1-255 characters')
  }
  // pass name to spawnPeer
  ```
- [Nit] Keep the tool guidance aligned with the new HTTP contract — the description still says a machine-spawn `message` field is stripped, but this diff now rejects it with HTTP 400. Agents using this description will reason about the wrong failure mode. Evidence `shared/src/sessionCitation.ts:32` and `hub/src/web/routes/machines.ts:94`.
  Suggested fix:
  ```ts
  'Do not call POST /api/machines/.../spawn with a message field - the hub rejects it. Use spawn_peer to create and deliver the remit. ' +
  ```

**Summary**
- Review mode: initial
- One deterministic CLI side-effect bug and one contradictory tool-description contract found.

**Testing**
- Not run (automation); GitHub `test` check passed at the reviewed head.
- Add a CLI test proving a 256-character `--name` fails before any spawn request.

*HAPI Bot*

**Findings**
- [Major] Wait for the fresh child to become active instead of resuming it — machine spawn returns when the runner receives the local session-started webhook, but the new hub row starts inactive and the asynchronously opened session socket is not awaited. The added pingPeer call treats that transient inactive state as a resume request, which can launch a second agent process for the same new session. Evidence cli/src/modules/spawnPeer/spawnPeer.ts:322; lifecycle context cli/src/agent/sessionFactory.ts:206, cli/src/modules/pingPeer/pingPeer.ts:506, cli/src/runner/run.ts:754.
  Suggested fix:
  ~~~ts
  pingResult = await pingPeer({
      sessionId,
      message,
      waitActiveSecs,
      waitForInitialActive: true,
      // ...
  })
  ~~~

**Summary**
- Review mode: follow-up after new commits
- One Major fresh-session lifecycle race found. The two prior bot findings no longer reproduce at this head.

**Testing**
- Not run (automation/security constraint); GitHub test check passed at this head.
- Add a test where the spawned session is initially inactive, then becomes active, and assert that /resume is never called.

*HAPI Bot*

**Findings**
- [Minor] Validate `permissionMode` against the selected agent before spawning — the new CLI/MCP inputs accept every global permission mode independently of `agent`. For example, `agent: 'codex', permissionMode: 'bypassPermissions'` passes this layer but the Codex command rejects the flag before its session webhook; `agent: 'pi'` silently drops every explicit mode in the runner. The call therefore either fails after launching a child or succeeds while ignoring an operator-visible request. Evidence `cli/src/modules/spawnPeer/spawnPeer.ts:267`; downstream constraints `cli/src/commands/codex.ts:72`, `cli/src/runner/run.ts:1543`, `shared/src/modes.ts:132`.
  Suggested fix:
  ```ts
  const flavor = options.agent ?? 'claude'
  if (
      options.permissionMode
      && !isPermissionModeAllowedForFlavor(options.permissionMode, flavor)
  ) {
      throw new SpawnPeerError(
          'bad_args',
          `permission mode ${options.permissionMode} is not supported by ${flavor}`
      )
  }
  ```

**Summary**
Review mode: follow-up after new commits
- One Minor flavor/mode validation issue found. The prior fresh-session duplicate-spawn finding is fixed at this head.

**Testing**
- Not run (automation/security constraint); GitHub `test` check was pending at review time.
- Add `spawnPeer` cases for an invalid Codex/Claude mode pairing and for Pi rejecting any explicit mode before the spawn request.

*HAPI Bot*

**Findings**
- [Minor] Validate `permissionMode` against the effective default agent - the new guard only runs when `options.agent` is explicit. When it is omitted, the hub defaults the spawn to Claude, so Claude-illegal values such as `yolo` or `read-only` pass this layer, start a child, and fail later in the Claude argument parser instead of being rejected as bad arguments. Evidence `cli/src/modules/spawnPeer/spawnPeer.ts:234`; defaulting context `hub/src/sync/syncEngine.ts:1804`, `cli/src/runner/run.ts:501`; downstream rejection `cli/src/commands/claude.ts:43`.
  Suggested fix:
  ```ts
  const flavor = options.agent ?? 'claude'
  if (
      options.permissionMode
      && !isPermissionModeAllowedForFlavor(options.permissionMode, flavor)
  ) {
      throw new SpawnPeerError(
          'bad_args',
          `permission mode ${options.permissionMode} is not supported by ${flavor}`
      )
  }
  ```

**Summary**
Review mode: follow-up after new commits
- One Minor validation issue remains when `agent` is omitted. The follow-up test covers only an explicit Codex pairing.

**Testing**
- Not run (automation/security constraint; PR code was not executed).
- GitHub `test` check was still in progress at review time.
- Add a no-`agent` case with a Claude-illegal mode and assert that no auth/spawn POST occurs.

*HAPI Bot*

**Findings**
- [Major] Resolve relative directories before crossing the runner boundary — `spawnPeer` forwards the caller string unchanged, but the machine RPC resolves relative paths in the long-lived runner process. A normal `hapi spawn-peer --dir .` or MCP relative path can therefore spawn in the directory where `hapi runner start` happened, not the calling session directory, potentially selecting the wrong repository. Evidence `cli/src/modules/spawnPeer/spawnPeer.ts:212`; runner context `cli/src/api/apiMachine.ts:390`, `cli/src/commands/runner.ts:147`.
  Suggested fix:
  ```ts
  import { resolve } from "node:path"

  const rawDirectory = (options.directory ?? "").trim()
  if (!rawDirectory) throw new SpawnPeerError("bad_args", "directory is required")
  const directory = resolve(rawDirectory)
  ```
- [Major] Roll back a spawned child when remit delivery fails — after machine spawn succeeds, both the `pingPeer` error path and the final verification timeout throw without stopping or archiving the new session. Retrying the advertised command creates another peer while the failed child (and any created worktree) remains active. Evidence `cli/src/modules/spawnPeer/spawnPeer.ts:346` and `cli/src/modules/spawnPeer/spawnPeer.ts:364`.
  Suggested fix:
  ```ts
  const archiveFailedSpawn = async () => {
      await http.post(
          `${apiUrl}/api/sessions/${encodeURIComponent(sessionId)}/archive`,
          {},
          { headers: authHeaders(jwt), validateStatus: () => true }
      ).catch(() => undefined)
  }

  // Call before rethrowing a delivery error and before the empty_session throw.
  await archiveFailedSpawn()
  ```

**Summary**
Review mode: follow-up after new commits
- The prior `permissionMode` finding is fixed in the latest commit. Two Major failure-mode/path-resolution issues remain in the full current diff.

**Testing**
- Not run (automation/security constraint; PR code was not executed).
- GitHub `test` and `pr-review` checks were pending at review time.
- Add coverage for `--dir .`/relative MCP paths and assert delivery/verification failures archive the spawned session exactly once.

*HAPI Bot*

**Findings**
- [Major] Retry transcript verification failures before cleanup — `sessionHasRemit` lets transport errors reject the whole operation, so one transient GET failure after a successful spawn bypasses `archiveFailedSpawn` and leaves a live child behind while CLI/MCP reports failure. Evidence `cli/src/modules/spawnPeer/spawnPeer.ts:205`.
  Suggested fix:
  ```ts
  async function sessionHasRemit(/* existing args */): Promise<boolean> {
      try {
          const response = await http.get(/* existing request */)
          // existing status/body matching
      } catch {
          return false // let the verification loop retry, then run cleanup
      }
  }
  ```
- [Minor] Do not report a requested name that was never applied — if rename fails, delivery throws after being accepted, and transcript reconciliation succeeds, `pingResult` is undefined and this fallback returns `requestedName` even though the hub rejected it. Evidence `cli/src/modules/spawnPeer/spawnPeer.ts:377`.
  Suggested fix:
  ```ts
  name: renamed
      ? requestedName
      : pingResult?.name || sessionId.slice(0, 8)
  ```

**Summary**
Review mode: follow-up after new commits
- The two prior cleanup findings are addressed. The latest head still has one cleanup-bypass regression and one inaccurate result field on ambiguous delivery recovery.

**Testing**
- Not run (automation/security constraint; PR code was not executed).
- GitHub `test` check passed; `pr-review` was pending at review time.
- Add coverage for a transcript GET that throws once then succeeds, and for rename failure plus an accepted-but-disconnected message POST.

*HAPI Bot*

**Findings**

**Summary**
Review mode: follow-up after new commits
- No additional correctness, security, regression, data-loss, performance, or maintainability issues found in the latest full diff.
- The prior transient transcript-verification and inaccurate rename-fallback findings are resolved at `cli/src/modules/spawnPeer/spawnPeer.ts:205` and `cli/src/modules/spawnPeer/spawnPeer.ts:382`, with regression coverage at `cli/src/modules/spawnPeer/spawnPeer.test.ts:542` and `cli/src/modules/spawnPeer/spawnPeer.test.ts:487`.

- [Major] Explicit permission modes are validated against Claude before the hub-selected agent is known — `cli/src/modules/spawnPeer/spawnPeer.ts:288`

p1468.title: feat(usage): record ACP cost and surface per-agent reporting availability

nodes.body:
**Findings**

- [Major] Preserve context across partial ACP usage updates — a `state_update` carrying tokens, or a cost-only `usage_update`, replaces the cached context fields with `undefined`. The final token event then becomes the newest usage event and the web context bar falls back to the input-token count instead of the previously reported context/window. Evidence `cli/src/agent/backends/acp/AcpSdkBackend.ts:858`.
  Suggested fix:
  ```ts
  const previous = this.latestUsageUpdate
  this.latestUsageUpdate = {
      contextTokens: contextTokens ?? previous?.contextTokens,
      contextWindow: contextWindow ?? previous?.contextWindow,
      tokenUsage: tokenUsage ?? previous?.tokenUsage ?? null,
      cost: cost ?? previous?.cost ?? null
  }
  ```

- [Major] Do not sum different currencies into one labeled scalar — cost parsing accepts any currency, but session costs are added together and labeled with whichever currency has the latest timestamp; per-agent totals have the same problem. For example, USD 1 plus EUR 1 can be returned as EUR 2. Evidence `hub/src/sync/usageService.ts:520` and related `hub/src/sync/usageService.ts:549`.
  Suggested fix:
  ```ts
  const costsByCurrency = new Map<string, number>()
  for (const cost of sessionCost.values()) {
      costsByCurrency.set(
          cost.currency,
          (costsByCurrency.get(cost.currency) ?? 0) + cost.amount
      )
  }
  // Return and display one amount per currency; do not collapse currencies.
  ```

- [Minor] Treat an explicit zero context as reported availability — `firstCount(...) > 0` cannot distinguish a missing field from `contextTokens: 0`, and it ignores `modelContextWindow`. A valid `{ contextTokens: 0, modelContextWindow: 200000 }` presence event is dropped and the agent is shown as `not-reported`. Evidence `hub/src/sync/usageService.ts:173`.
  Suggested fix:
  ```ts
  const contextTokens = asCount(info.contextTokens ?? info.context_tokens)
  const contextWindow = asCount(info.modelContextWindow ?? info.model_context_window)
  const contextOnly = !hasProcessedTokens
      && (contextTokens !== null || contextWindow !== null)
  ```

**Summary**

Two Major correctness findings and one Minor availability-classification finding. No questions required.

This turns nonzero usage into an apparent zero on both the total and per-agent displays. Evidence `web/src/routes/settings/usage.tsx:18`.
  Suggested fix:

  const precision = amount > 0 && amount < 0.01
      ? { minimumSignificantDigits: 2, maximumSignificantDigits: 4 }

**Findings**

- [Minor] Preserve sub-cent cost precision — currency formatting defaults to the currency's standard fraction digits, so a legitimate cumulative cost such as USD 0.004 renders as $0.00. This presents nonzero usage as zero in both the total and per-agent displays. Evidence `web/src/routes/settings/usage.tsx:20`.

  Suggested fix:
  ```ts
  const precision = amount > 0 && amount < 0.01
      ? { minimumSignificantDigits: 2, maximumSignificantDigits: 4 }
      : {}
  return new Intl.NumberFormat(undefined, {
      style: 'currency',
      currency,
      ...precision
  }).format(amount)
  ```

*HAPI Bot*

**Findings**

- [Minor] Derive the small-amount threshold from the currency — the hard-coded `0.01` only protects two-decimal currencies. For a zero-decimal currency such as JPY, a valid amount like `0.4` takes the default branch and renders as `¥0`, again presenting nonzero spend as zero. Evidence `web/src/routes/settings/usage.tsx:22`.

  Suggested fix:
  ```ts
  const base = new Intl.NumberFormat(undefined, { style: 'currency', currency })
  const smallestUnit = 10 ** -base.resolvedOptions().maximumFractionDigits
  const precision = amount > 0 && amount < smallestUnit
      ? { minimumSignificantDigits: 2, maximumSignificantDigits: 4 }
      : {}
  return new Intl.NumberFormat(undefined, { style: 'currency', currency, ...precision }).format(amount)
  ```

- [Minor] Declare the cost fields on the exported wire type — `convertAgentMessage` now emits `cost` and `costCurrency`, but the `token_count` member of `CodexMessage` does not expose them. The conditional spread bypasses excess-property checking, so narrowed typed callers cannot read the fields that are present at runtime. Evidence `cli/src/agent/messageConverter.ts:73`.

  Suggested fix:

  type: 'token_count'

  ```

  ```ts
  let previous = baseline

          amount += point.amount >= previous.amount
              ? point.amount - previous.amount
              : point.amount
      } else if (!previous && (from === null || session.createdAt >= from)) {
          amount += point.amount
      }
      previous = point
  }
  ```

**Findings**
- [Major] Same-tab consumers never receive the new preference — `setPinActiveSessions` updates only its own hook instance and localStorage, while `storage` events fire only in other documents. The router keeps `SessionList` mounted alongside the settings outlet, so toggling this switch does not move active sessions until the app is reloaded.   Suggested fix:
  ```ts
  const CHANGE_EVENT = 'hapi-pin-active-sessions-change'

  const onLocalChange = (event: Event) => {
      if (event instanceof CustomEvent && typeof event.detail === 'boolean') {
          setPinActiveSessionsState(event.detail)
      }
  }
  window.addEventListener(CHANGE_EVENT, onLocalChange)

  // After persisting in setPinActiveSessions.
  window.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent(CHANGE_EVENT, { detail: value }))

  Remove the local listener during effect cleanup, and add a test mounting two hook consumers to verify that changing one updates the other immediately.

Cursor returns steer success after stdin dispatch while keeping the reservation dispatching until the ACP response completes; the same tab can therefore re-enable Cancel, stamp the row invoked, then restore it to the CLI queue if ACP later rejects. A restart in that state loses the prompt. Evidence `cli/src/utils/MessageQueue2.ts:280`, related context `hub/src/sync/messageService.ts:502` and `cli/src/cursor/cursorAcpRemoteLauncher.ts:390`.
  Suggested fix:
  ```ts
  type CancelQueueResult = 'removed' | 'missing' | 'busy'
  if (reservation.state === 'dispatching') return 'busy'
  ```
  Propagate `busy` through the socket ack and have the Hub return a retryable conflict without deleting the row or setting `invoked_at`.
- [Minor] The web availability gate trusts persisted `steeringActive` without checking whether the session is still active/remote. An abrupt CLI exit leaves agent state untouched, so an inactive session with queued work can show an enabled Steer button even though the route requires an active session. Evidence `web/src/components/SessionChat.tsx:1816`.

        echoCancellation: true,
        noiseSuppression: true,
        autoGainControl: true
    }
})
```

to:

```ts
navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia({ audio: true })
```

This change appears unrelated to the session-navigation behavior addressed by
this PR. It also makes standard dictation inconsistent with the realtime
transcription paths, which still request all three microphone constraints.

The maintained `v0.29.0.3` PWA carries this PR head and exposes the issue on
mobile. The code regression is confirmed; whether it fully explains the
reported recognition degradation still needs a Standard/Realtime A/B test.

Could the original microphone constraints be preserved and a regression test
added to assert the `getUserMedia` arguments?

  const activeEvents = selectActiveClaudeBranch(parsedEvents)

nodes.body:
**Findings**

- [Major] Direct send races transcript finalization - the added handler can submit stale or empty composer text before dictation finishes; see the inline comment at `web/src/components/AssistantChat/ComposerButtons.tsx:514`.

**Summary**

Review mode: initial

One Major issue found. The new direct voice-send path does not wait for the final standard/realtime dictation transcript, so the spoken result can remain unsent.

**Testing**

- Not run (automation; PR code was not executed).
- GitHub `test` and `pr-review` checks were pending at review time.
- Added component coverage uses synchronous callback spies; async transcript-finalization coverage is missing for standard and realtime dictation.

*HAPI Bot*

**Findings**

- [Blocker] The PR fails TypeScript validation — changing the standard dictation toggle to return `Promise<boolean>` makes `result.current.toggle()` infer as `Promise<boolean> | Promise<void>`, which is not a valid direct return from React Testing Library's `act`. The current `test` check fails with TS2769 at `web/src/hooks/useDictation.test.ts:55`, `:57`, `:102`, `:164`, and `:169`; `:102` is added by this PR.
  Suggested fix:
  ```ts
  await act(async () => {
      await result.current.toggle()
  })
  ```
  Apply this wrapper form to all five direct `act(() => result.current.toggle())` calls.

- [Major] Realtime dictation still treats cancellation and failure as a committed transcript — the new handler sends for every result except literal `false`, while `useRealtimeDictation.toggle()` always resolves `void`. During the visible `connecting` state, a click can abort startup with no session and then submit the existing draft; a realtime stop error likewise calls `fail()` but still resolves `void` and submits. Evidence `web/src/components/AssistantChat/ComposerButtons.tsx:519`, related context `web/src/hooks/useRealtimeDictation.ts:204`.
  Suggested fix:
  ```tsx
  const committed = await props.onVoiceToggle()
  if (committed === true) {
      props.onSend('default')
  }
  ```
  Make realtime `stop`/`toggle` return `Promise<boolean>`: `false` when no session exists or an error/cancel occurs, and `true` only after `onFinalTranscript` inserts a non-empty final transcript.

**Summary**

Review mode: follow-up after new commits

One Blocker and one Major remain at the latest head. The current head cannot pass typecheck, and realtime direct-send can submit without a successful transcription.

**Testing**

- Not run (automation; PR code was not executed).
- GitHub `test` fails in `bun typecheck` with TS2769.
- Add realtime direct-send coverage for connecting cancellation, stop failure, empty final transcript, and successful finalization.

*HAPI Bot*

**Findings**

- [Blocker] Voice-state transitions change the hook count - the new early return runs before `useLongPress`, so a disconnected -> connecting/connected render skips hooks that were called previously and React can throw "Rendered fewer hooks than expected." Evidence `web/src/components/AssistantChat/ComposerButtons.tsx:507`.
  Suggested fix:
  ```tsx
  const canQueueGesture = Boolean(
      props.allowQueueGesture
      && hasText
      && !isVoiceActive
      && !routesToScratchlist
      && !props.controlsDisabled
  )
  const sendButtonHandlers = useLongPress(existingOptions)

  if (isVoiceActive) {
      return voiceButtons
  }
  ```

- [Major] Realtime cancellation and stop failures still submit the draft - `committed !== false` treats the realtime toggle's `undefined` result as success. A Send click while connecting aborts with no session, and a stop error calls `fail()`; both then invoke `onSend`. Evidence `web/src/components/AssistantChat/ComposerButtons.tsx:520`, related context `web/src/hooks/useRealtimeDictation.ts:204`.
  Suggested fix:
  ```tsx
  const committed = await props.onVoiceToggle()
  if (committed === true) {
      props.onSend('default')
  }
  ```

**Findings**

- [Major] Register the custom session MIME as an allowed drop target — the editor installs `onDrop`, but no `dragover` handler cancels the browser default for `application/x-hapi-session-mention`. The bubbling `DragDropZone` only accepts `Files`, so a real browser can keep the drag operation at `none` and never dispatch this drop. The current unit test calls `fireEvent.drop` directly and bypasses that prerequisite. Evidence: `web/src/components/AssistantChat/RichComposerInput.tsx:1153`.

  Suggested fix:
  ```tsx
  const handleDragOver = useCallback((e: React.DragEvent<HTMLDivElement>) => {
      if (disabled || !e.dataTransfer.types.includes(SESSION_MENTION_DRAG_MIME)) return
      e.preventDefault()
      e.dataTransfer.dropEffect = 'copy'
  }, [disabled])

  // editor props
  onDragOver={handleDragOver}
  onDrop={handleDrop}
  ```

- [Minor] Place the mention at the drop point — `insertSessionMention` reads the current window selection, but this handler never derives a caret from `e.clientX/e.clientY`. After dragging from the session-row button, that selection is stale or outside the editor; the existing selection mapper then falls back to EOF. Dropping over the middle of existing text therefore appends at the end or uses an old caret. Evidence: `web/src/components/AssistantChat/RichComposerInput.tsx:987`.

  Suggested fix:
  ```tsx
  const range = document.caretRangeFromPoint?.(e.clientX, e.clientY)
  const root = rootRef.current
  if (range && root?.contains(range.startContainer)) {
      root.focus()
      const selection = window.getSelection()
      selection?.removeAllRanges()
      selection?.addRange(range)
  }
  onSessionMentionDrop?.(mention)
  ```

**Summary**

**Findings**

- [Minor] Support Firefox caret hit-testing — `document.caretRangeFromPoint` is the WebKit/Chromium API; Firefox exposes `caretPositionFromPoint`. Drops over existing text therefore still insert at EOF. Evidence: `web/src/components/AssistantChat/RichComposerInput.tsx:994`.

nodes.body:
**Findings**

- [Major] Cross-origin clients cannot save either notification setting - both new mutation routes use `PUT`, but the hub's CORS policy allows only `GET`, `POST`, `PATCH`, `DELETE`, and `OPTIONS`. In relay and standalone deployments the official/static web app is a different origin, so browser preflight blocks preference toggles and copy saves before they reach the hub. Evidence: `hub/src/web/routes/notificationPreferences.ts:21` (also `hub/src/web/routes/notificationCopy.ts:33`), with CORS context at `hub/src/web/server.ts:240`.
  Suggested fix:
  ```ts
  allowMethods: ['GET', 'POST', 'PUT', 'PATCH', 'DELETE', 'OPTIONS'],
  ```

- [Major] Editing before copy hydration can erase existing templates - the admin editor renders enabled with an empty draft while `copyQuery` is pending. Any early edit sets `userEditedRef`, causing the fetched config to be discarded; Save then sends only that partial draft, and the route replaces the complete persisted `notificationCopy` object. Existing templates in every untouched block (and possibly the untouched field in the edited block) are silently lost. Evidence: `web/src/routes/settings/notifications.tsx:104`.
  Suggested fix:
  ```tsx
  {isAdmin && copyQuery.isSuccess ? (
      <SettingsSection>{/* existing copy editor */}</SettingsSection>
  ) : null}
  ```

**Summary**

Review mode: follow-up after new commits

The previous three findings are resolved. Two remaining major issues affect cross-origin saving and preservation of existing notification-copy configuration.

**Testing**

Not run (review automation; PR code was not executed). The live GitHub `test` check passes. Add a CORS preflight test for `PUT` and a UI regression test that delays `getNotificationCopy`, attempts an early edit, and verifies existing templates cannot be overwritten.

*HAPI Bot*

**Findings**

- [Major] Serialize runtime updates to settings.json - the new copy endpoint performs an unlocked read-modify-write. A concurrent copy save or relay-key refresh can read the same snapshot and overwrite the other update; because writeSettings also shares one .tmp path, overlapping writes can rename each other's temporary file and fail. This can silently remove notificationCopy or relayAuthKey. Evidence: hub/src/web/routes/notificationCopy.ts:45 (related writers: hub/src/tunnel/relayAuth.ts:83, hub/src/config/settings.ts:72).
  Suggested fix:
  ~~~ts
  await mutateSettings(settingsFile, (settings) => {
      settings.notificationCopy = copy
  })
  ~~~
  Make mutateSettings serialize the complete read-modify-write operation per settings path.

- [Minor] Surface copy-save failures - unlike preference saves, this mutation has no onError state or rendered error. Offline, parse, or filesystem failures simply re-enable Save while leaving the user with no indication that the templates were not persisted. Evidence: web/src/routes/settings/notifications.tsx:140.
  Suggested fix:
  ~~~tsx
  onError: () => {
      setCopySaveError(t('settings.notifications.copy.saveError'))
  },
  ~~~
  Render copySaveError next to the Save action and clear it on the next attempt/success.

**Summary**

Review mode: follow-up after new commits

The previous CORS and pre-hydration overwrite findings are resolved at the current head. Two remaining issues affect durable settings updates and copy-save error reporting.

**Testing**

Not run (automation; PR code was not executed). GitHub checks were pending at review time. Add a concurrent settings mutation test covering copy plus relay-key writes, and a UI test for a rejected updateNotificationCopy request.

*HAPI Bot*

**Findings**

- [Minor] Clear the copy editor dirty latch after a successful save — userEditedRef is set on the first edit but never reset. After one save, later query refetches from another tab/device are permanently ignored, and the next full-config PUT can overwrite those newer hub-wide templates. Evidence web/src/routes/settings/notifications.tsx:149
  Suggested fix:
  ~~~tsx
  onSuccess: (data) => {
      userEditedRef.current = false
      queryClient.setQueryData(queryKeys.notificationCopy, data)
      // ...
  },
  ~~~

- [Minor] Await the confirmed permission update — the async callback starts mutation.mutate() and resolves immediately, so ConfirmDialog closes before the request completes and its pending/error contract cannot work. A failed disable therefore dismisses the confirmation as though it completed. Evidence web/src/routes/settings/notifications.tsx:338
  Suggested fix:
  ~~~tsx
  onConfirm={() => mutation.mutateAsync({ permissionRequests: 0 })}
  ~~~

- [Minor] Enforce binary preference values — min(0).max(1) accepts values such as 0.5, which are persisted and returned even though the store/UI contract is a 0-or-1 switch. The notification gate then silently treats any fraction as enabled. Evidence hub/src/web/routes/notificationPreferences.ts:7
  Suggested fix:
  ~~~ts
  const notificationFlagSchema = z.number().int().min(0).max(1)
  ~~~

**Summary**

p1351.title: feat(claude): steer mid-turn messages instead of queueing them

nodes.body:
**Findings**

- [Major] Preserve isolation for the current in-flight command - the steering guard checks the incoming message and mode, but not whether the turn already running is isolated. Once an isolated `/compact` batch is handed to the SDK, `turnInFlight` is true and a normal `steer=true` message with the same mode passes this guard, so it is injected into the isolated command instead of queued. Evidence: `cli/src/claude/claudeRemoteLauncher.ts:449`.

  Suggested fix:

  ```ts
  if (inFlightMessage?.isolate) return false
  if (!modeHash || session.queue.hashMode(messageMode) !== modeHash) return false
  ```

- [Minor] Correct the alternate-shortcut hint for "Insert newline" mode - in that mode Ctrl/Cmd+Enter is the primary send shortcut and Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+Enter is the alternate (`web/src/components/AssistantChat/HappyComposer.tsx:1007`), so telling users to "Add Ctrl" points them to the primary behavior instead. Evidence: `web/src/lib/locales/en.ts:732`, `web/src/lib/locales/zh-CN.ts:736`.

  Suggested fix:

  ```ts
  'settings.chat.steerBehavior.hint':
      'Use Ctrl/Cmd+Enter - or Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+Enter when Enter inserts a newline - to use the other behavior for one message. Claude sessions only.',
  ```

**Summary**

Review mode: initial

2 findings: 1 Major correctness issue and 1 Minor user-facing shortcut issue. Residual risk remains around real Claude stream delivery and crash recovery because the launcher tests mock `claudeRemote`.

- [Major] Prepend trimming can retain sidechain rows after their owning Task row is dropped — the orphan boundary only handles the old edge of the window. Evidence: `web/src/lib/message-window-store.ts:512`.

**Summary**

**Testing**
- Not run (automation); PR-provided code was not executed.

*HAPI Bot*

**Findings**
- [Major] Deferred sidechain recovery is lost across sessionStorage hydration; see inline comment.
- [Major] The prepend high-sequence cutoff drops sidechain children whose Task parent is still retained; see inline comment.

**Questions**

- Review mode: follow-up after new commits
- Two correctness issues remain in the revised overflow handling. Both can leave Task-card history incomplete; one survives page reload with no recovery path.

Both findings were real. Fixed in 6957978.

**Sidechain-only tail truncation has no recoverable state** — correct, and the second half of that is the more serious one: suppressing the reset kept the reader in place but left nothing to ever refetch the missing transcript, so a Task card could stay permanently incomplete.

The suppression is now a *deferral*. `sidechainOverflowed` records that the window is short, and `enterTailMode` redeems it into `requiresLatestReset` — that being exactly the moment the reader chose to come back to the tail, so the refetch costs them nothing. `activateMessageWindow`'s early-return had to learn about the flag too, or re-opening the session would skip the redemption.

The reset condition itself was also the wrong shape. Comparing newest positions meant "no top-level rows at all" fell through to a reset on every overflow. It now reads the dropped set directly — *did any top-level row leave?* — which answers the question the flag actually asks and behaves consistently for a sidechain-only window.

**Prepend trimming can retain sidechain rows after their owning Task row is dropped** — also correct, I only guarded the old edge. Prepend drops the newest top-level rows, so a subagent that started after the last survivor has lost its parent too, and `tracer.ts:139` renders those at the top level.

Both edges are now enforced, with the new edge applied *only* under prepend. Under append it would be actively wrong: a subagent running right now legitimately sits past every top-level row, and cutting there would empty the live Task card.

**Coverage** for the three gaps called out, each verified to fail when its own logic is disabled:

- `refetches the latest page when returning to the tail after a subagent overflow` — history → overflow → tail, asserts the epoch is cleared
- `drops subagent messages left past the newest surviving top-level row` — prepend overflow with the parent Task trimmed
- `handles a window that holds nothing but subagent messages` — sidechain-only overflow

`34 passed` in this file. Full suite shows no change against baseline (same 128 environment-related failures before and after, +3 passing = the new tests). `bun run typecheck` clean.

*HAPI Bot*

Both findings were real. Fixed in the latest commit.

**[Major] stale offline-inclusive cache** — worse than it first looked. Machine liveness does not travel through invalidation at all; `upsertMachine` writes directly via `setQueryData` against the exact `['machines']` key, so `['machines', 'withOffline']` was never touched. My claim in the PR description that prefix-based invalidation covers it was wrong for this path: prefix matching only helps the `invalidateQueries` call at `useSSE.ts:316`, and liveness never goes through it.

Writing to both keys would not have been enough either, because the two caches disagree about what offline means — the online-only list *drops* a machine that goes offline, while the settings list must *keep* it and render it as offline. So the fold is now an exported pure function with an explicit contract:

```ts
applyMachineToCache(previous, machine, { keepOffline: boolean })
```

applied once per cache, with the deletion path writing to both keys as well. Being a pure export makes it directly testable, matching how `isRenderIrrelevantPatch` and friends are already tested in that file. 8 new cases cover both contracts; I verified they bite by making the function ignore `keepOffline` — exactly the two offline-inclusive cases fail.

**[Minor] status hidden from assistive tech** — correct, the dot was `aria-hidden` with no text alternative. It now carries `role="img"` with a localised name (Online / Offline, en + zh-CN) plus a matching `title`, and there is a test asserting both are reachable by accessible name.

p1126.title: fix(web): preserve loaded history during streaming

nodes.body:
**Findings**
- [Major] Scrolled-up streaming window is now unbounded — why it matters: while the user is reading older history, every agent SSE merge appends into `messages` without any trim. This store feeds `SessionChat`/`HappyThread` directly, so a long-running stream can keep growing the rendered thread until the user returns to the bottom. The previous code kept the live window bounded; this PR should preserve the loaded older page without removing the cap entirely. Evidence `web/src/lib/message-window-store.ts:1041`.
  Suggested fix:
  ```ts
  const messages = mergeMessages(state.messages, agentMessages)
  const { kept, dropped } = trimPreservingQueued(
      messages,
      OLDER_LOAD_WINDOW_SIZE + VISIBLE_WINDOW_SIZE,
      'append'
  )
  const pending = filterPendingAgainstVisible(state.pending, kept)
  state = buildState(state, {
      messages: kept,
      pending,
      ...cursorUpdatesAfterAppendTrim(kept, dropped)
  })
  ```

p1092.title: feat(workspace): add scoped file and Git controls

nodes.body:
**Findings**
- [Major] `create-file` accepts unbounded content — `HostFileWriteRequestSchema` caps text writes at 2 MiB and uploads at 20 MiB, but the generic host operation schema accepts any-size `content` for `create-file` and `FileManager` writes it directly. An authenticated client can bypass the new file-size limits through `/host/operations`, forcing the hub/runner to parse and write an arbitrarily large JSON string. Evidence: `shared/src/workspaceManagement.ts:129`, `cli/src/host/fileManager.ts:255`.
  Suggested fix:
  ```ts
  const MAX_HOST_FILE_CREATE_BYTES = 2 * 1024 * 1024

  content: z.string().max(MAX_HOST_FILE_CREATE_BYTES).optional()
  ```

- [Minor] Download chunks can spin forever after a source file shrinks — `readChunk()` treats a zero-byte read as success even when `remaining > 0`, returning the same `nextOffset` with `done: false`. The web loop will keep requesting the same offset until the user leaves the page. Evidence: `cli/src/host/downloadManager.ts:151`.
  Suggested fix:
  ```ts
  const { bytesRead } = await handle.read(buffer, 0, bytes, offset)
  if (bytesRead === 0) {
      return { success: false, error: 'Download changed while being read' }
  }
  ```

**Questions**
- None.

**Summary**
- Review mode: follow-up after new commits
- The previous `.git` metadata findings appear addressed in the latest head. I found two remaining issues in the latest PR diff: an unbounded create-file payload path and a download edge case that can trap the client polling loop.

**Testing**
- Not run (review-only automation). Suggested coverage: schema test rejecting oversized `create-file.content`; download test where the prepared file is truncated before `readChunk()`.

*HAPI Bot*

**Findings**
- [Major] Reject option-like remote names before shelling out — `GitRemoteNameSchema` accepts leading dashes, so values like `--all` pass API validation and then reach `git push`/`git fetch` as the remote argument. Git parses those as options, which can make a machine-scoped request operate on a broader target than the selected remote. Evidence `shared/src/workspaceManagement.ts:226`; call sites `cli/src/host/repositoryManager.ts:292`, `cli/src/host/repositoryManager.ts:316`, `cli/src/host/repositoryManager.ts:356`.
  Suggested fix:
  ```ts
  const GitRemoteNameSchema = z.string()
      .trim()
      .min(1)
      .regex(/^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$/)
      .refine((value) => !value.startsWith('-') && value !== '.' && value !== '..', 'Invalid remote name')
  ```

**Questions**
- None.

**Summary**
- Review mode: follow-up after new commits
- The previous `.git` preview and prepared-download retargeting findings appear addressed in the current diff. Remaining issue: Git remote names need option-like value rejection before CLI execution.

**Testing**
- Not run (automation; PR-content execution disabled). Suggested coverage: schema tests rejecting `remote: "--all"` and `remote: "-n"` for push/fetch/set-remote/delete-remote-branch.

*HAPI Bot*

**Findings**
- [Major] Allow valid slash-separated branch names — `GitBranchNameSchema` rejects `/`, so branch operations for common names like `feature/workspace-controls` fail hub-side validation before reaching the runner. Evidence: the schema rejects slash at `shared/src/workspaceManagement.ts:235`, while the new schema test expects `feature/workspace-controls` to parse at `shared/src/workspaceManagement.test.ts:19` and the web sends Git-listed branch names back for switch/delete at `web/src/components/WorkspaceBrowser.tsx:557`.
  Suggested fix:
  ```ts
  const GitBranchNameSchema = z.string().trim().min(1).max(255).refine((value) => {
      if (value.startsWith('-') || value === '@' || value.includes('@{')) return false
      if (value.includes('..') || value.includes('//') || value.endsWith('.') || value.endsWith('/')) return false
      if (/[\x00-\x20\x7f~^:?*\\[\]]/.test(value)) return false
      return value.split('/').every((part) => part && !part.startsWith('.') && !part.endsWith('.lock'))
  }, 'Invalid branch name')
  ```

**Questions**
- None.

**Summary**
- Review mode: follow-up after new commits
- The previous option-like remote-name issue is addressed, but the current schema still blocks ordinary slash-separated Git branch names and contradicts the added schema test.

**Testing**
- Not run (automation; PR-content execution disabled). Suggested coverage: keep the existing `feature/workspace-controls` schema assertion and add a negative case for invalid double-slash branch names.

*HAPI Bot*

**Findings**
- None.

**Questions**
- None.

**Findings**
- [Major] `.git` symlink targets can still receive file writes — `upload()` resolves `request.directory` with `resolveReadable()`, which follows symlinks before any `.git` segment rejection. With a workspace entry like `.git -> metadata`, a request for `directory: "<root>/.git", name: "config"` canonicalizes to `<root>/metadata/config` and writes there. `copyOrMove()` uses the same generic readable resolution for destination directories, so copy/move can write into the same target. This violates the file-plane Git metadata boundary. Evidence `cli/src/host/fileManager.ts:201`, `cli/src/host/fileManager.ts:306`
  Suggested fix:
  ```ts
  const directory = await this.scope.resolveReadableNonGitMetadata(request.directory)

  // copy/move existing destination path
  destinationDirectory = await this.scope.resolveReadableNonGitMetadata(operation.destination)

  // lock key for copy/move existing destination path
  : await this.scope.resolveReadableNonGitMetadata(operation.destination)
  ```

**Findings**
- [Major] Host upload bodies are parsed before any request-size limit, so the shared schema cap is reached only after the hub has already buffered the full JSON body. Evidence `hub/src/web/routes/machines.ts:132`.
  Suggested fix:
  ```ts
  import { bodyLimit } from "hono/body-limit"
  import { MAX_HOST_FILE_UPLOAD_BYTES } from "@hapi/protocol"

  const HOST_UPLOAD_JSON_BYTES = Math.ceil((MAX_HOST_FILE_UPLOAD_BYTES * 4) / 3) + 8192
  const hostBodyLimit = bodyLimit({
      maxSize: HOST_UPLOAD_JSON_BYTES,
      onError: (c) => c.json({ error: "Payload too large" }, 413)

- [Major] Directory archive limits count files only, not archive entries, so a workspace tree with many empty directories can still force unbounded traversal and ZIP metadata generation. Evidence `cli/src/host/downloadManager.ts:87`.
  Suggested fix:
  ```ts
  const MAX_ARCHIVE_ENTRIES = 20_000
  let entries = 0

  function countArchiveEntry(): void {
      entries += 1
      if (entries > MAX_ARCHIVE_ENTRIES) {
          throw new Error(`Directory contains more than ${MAX_ARCHIVE_ENTRIES} entries`)
      }
  }

  // Before zip.addEmptyDirectory(...)
  countArchiveEntry()

  // Before zip.addReadStream(...)

  ```

Local clone sources and set-remote paths, including `file:` URLs and relative paths, now resolve through WorkspaceScope before reaching Git. Network URLs and GitHub shorthand remain supported. Added focused `.git` visibility/preview and symlink-retarget regressions.

p1091.title: feat(providers): add managed agent API profiles

nodes.body:
**Findings**
- [Major] `--hapi-provider system` removes native credentials before launch — the explicit system override should bypass managed profiles and let Claude/Codex/Grok use the user's normal env/login, but `applyProviderSelection()` calls `clearConflictingCredentials(agent)` before handling `requestedId === null`. That path is used by terminal launches and local resume of sessions whose metadata stores `providerProfileId: null`, so it deletes `ANTHROPIC_*`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, or `XAI_*` before the agent process is spawned. Evidence `cli/src/host/applyProviderSelection.ts:36`
  Suggested fix:
  ```typescript
  if (requestedId !== undefined) {
      clearProviderMetadata()
      if (requestedId === null) {
          process.env.HAPI_PROVIDER_PROFILE_SYSTEM = '1'
          return null
      }
  }

  const profile = await new ProviderRegistry().resolve(agent, requestedId)
  if (!profile) return null

  const launch = resolveProviderLaunch(agent, profile)
  clearProviderMetadata()
  clearConflictingCredentials(agent)
  ```

The session model picker can split the native catalog into duplicate groups when the persisted model is no longer returned by the catalog. `mergeModelOptions()` inserts a synthetic `Current` row at index 1, so the rendered order becomes `Native → model → Current → persisted model → Native → …`.

I do not think the session picker needs either a `Current` fallback category or source-group headers: the selected radio state already communicates the current choice. Removing the Pi-only panel makes Pi sessions use the unified model list, but that list still keys and highlights rows by bare `modelId`; the repo explicitly preserves `metadata.piSelectedModel` because two providers can share the same model id. With duplicate IDs, React can reuse duplicate keys and the UI marks every matching `modelId` as selected, so users cannot tell which provider-backed model is active before changing it. Evidence: `web/src/components/AssistantChat/HappyComposer.tsx:798`, related context `web/src/components/AssistantChat/HappyComposer.tsx:898` and `web/src/components/AssistantChat/HappyComposer.tsx:911`.

  const isPiModelSelected = (piModel: PiModelSummary) => selectedPiModel

The same state also shows unfiltered thinking levels before `selectedPiModel` is known. Evidence `web/src/components/AssistantChat/HappyComposer.tsx:796`.

The Bridge ID is predictable from the displayed event ID; a client message arriving after Bridge enqueue with the allowed `bridge:<eventId>` local ID can therefore be acknowledged before it runs, removed from durable replay/cancel state, and silently lost if the CLI exits. Evidence `cli/src/cursor/cursorAcpRemoteLauncher.ts:1056`, `cli/src/utils/MessageQueue2.ts:426`, `hub/src/socket/handlers/cli/sessionHandlers.ts:383`.

  )

A newer correction queued during that window is invisible to this check, so the stale Bridge runs first. Evidence `cli/src/cursor/cursorAcpRemoteLauncher.ts:506`, with dispatch at `cli/src/cursor/cursorAcpRemoteLauncher.ts:571`.

  const sent = await backend.prompt(acpSessionId, promptContent, onUpdate, {

Evidence `cli/src/cursor/cursorAgentMessageClassifier.ts:337`.

  if (STRONG_STDERR_PATTERNS.rate_limit.test(raw)) {

      PERMISSION_REQUEST("permission-request"),
      TASK_NOTIFICATION("task-notification"),

p975.title: feat: add OMP (Oh My Pi) coding agent support

nodes.body:
**Findings**
- [Blocker] OMP web launches still spawn Claude — adding `omp` to the shared flavor list makes it selectable in New Session, but runner spawn argument construction has no `omp` branch, so `buildCliArgs('omp', ...)` falls through to `claude`. Creating an OMP session from the web/runner will start Claude instead of `hapi omp`. Evidence `shared/src/modes.ts:10`, related context `cli/src/runner/run.ts:1076`.
  Suggested fix:
  ```ts
  const agentCommand = agent === 'codex'
      ? 'codex'
      : agent === 'cursor'
          ? 'cursor'
          : agent === 'gemini'
              ? 'gemini'
              : agent === 'kimi'
                  ? 'kimi'
                  : agent === 'opencode'
                      ? 'opencode'
                      : agent === 'pi'
                          ? 'pi'
                          : agent === 'omp'
                              ? 'omp'
                              : 'claude'

  if (options.effort && (agent === 'claude' || agent === 'pi' || agent === 'omp')) {
      args.push('--effort', options.effort)
  }
  ```

- [Major] OMP resume metadata is written but not used by resume flows — this PR adds `ompSessionId`, but `resolveAgentResumeId()` and the web-side `resolveAgentSessionIdFromMetadata()` still fall through to Claude for `flavor === 'omp'`; `hapi resume` also has no OMP dispatch branch and would fall through to Cursor once the hub starts returning OMP targets. Inactive OMP sessions with messages therefore show/return resume unavailable instead of using the stored OMP id. Evidence `shared/src/schemas.ts:53`, related context `hub/src/sync/syncEngine.ts:752` and `cli/src/commands/resume.ts:165`.
  Suggested fix:
  ```ts
  // hub/src/sync/syncEngine.ts
  if (flavor === 'omp') return metadata.ompSessionId ?? null

  // web/src/lib/sessionResume.ts
  case 'omp': return metadata.ompSessionId ?? undefined

  // cli/src/commands/resume.ts
  if (target.flavor === 'omp') {
      const { runOmp } = await import('@/omp/runOmp')
      await runOmp({
          existingSessionId: base.existingSessionId,
          workingDirectory: base.workingDirectory,
          resumeSessionId: base.resumeSessionId,
          startedBy: base.startedBy,
          startingMode: 'remote',
          model: target.model ?? undefined,
          effort: target.effort ?? undefined,
      })
      return
  }
  ```

**Summary**
- Review mode: initial
- OMP core loop has coverage, but the flavor is not fully wired into runner spawn/resume entrypoints yet.

*HAPI Bot*

**Findings**
- [Major] OMP resume silently creates a fresh conversation when exact restore fails — when `switch_session` rejects or times out, this fallback sends `new_session` inside the existing HAPI session row. **Findings**
- [Major] Preserve transcript timestamps during direct import — `importSingleSession` writes every imported row through `addMessage`, so `created_at`/`invoked_at` are stamped with the import time rather than the Claude row timestamp. The hub then sorts sessions by `updatedAt` and message pages by `invokedAt ?? createdAt`, so importing an old Claude transcript makes it look active today and collapses historical message timing. Claude JSONL rows already expose `timestamp` (see existing `RawJSONLinesBaseSchema`), but the new Claude importer drops it before persistence. Evidence: `hub/src/web/routes/transcriptImport.ts:805`.
  Suggested fix:
  ```ts
  type ImportedTranscriptMessage = {
      content: ImportedMessageContent
      createdAt?: number
  }

  function parseClaudeTimestamp(record: Record<string, unknown>): number | undefined {
      if (typeof record.timestamp !== 'string') return undefined
      const value = Date.parse(record.timestamp)
      return Number.isFinite(value) ? value : undefined
  }

  const createdAt = message.createdAt ?? transcript.modifiedAt
  const appendedMessages = messagesToAppend.map((message) =>
      options.store.messages.copyMessageToSession(sessionId!, {
          content: message.content,
          createdAt,
          invokedAt: createdAt,
          localId: undefined,
          scheduledAt: null
      })
  )
  ```

Evidence: `cli/src/codex/utils/codexUsage.ts:56`, `cli/src/codex/utils/codexUsage.ts:84`.
  Suggested fix:
  ```ts
  const direct = record.resets_at ?? record.resetsAt ?? record.reset_at ?? record.resetAt

      'window_duration_mins',
      'windowDurationMins',
      'window_minutes',
      'windowMinutes'
  ])
  ```

- [Major] Sparse account updates are applied as full replacements — account rate-limit notifications may contain only the changed bucket/account fields, but every payload with a rate-limit snapshot replaces all buckets and deletes every omitted credit/plan/limit field. A primary-only update can therefore erase a still-valid weekly bucket and credit state. Evidence: `cli/src/codex/utils/appServerEventConverter.ts:667`, `cli/src/codex/session.ts:175`.
  Suggested fix:
  ```ts
  const replace = update.rateLimitMode === 'replace'
  const merged = {
      ...previous,
      ...usage,
      rateLimits: replace
          ? usage.rateLimits
          : { ...previous?.rateLimits, ...usage.rateLimits }
  }
  if (replace || usage.credits !== undefined) {
      // replace/clear only for full snapshots; patch account updates otherwise
  }
  ```

Hi @heavygee — the usage indicator from this PR has a bug worth fixing before merge: **the rate-limit buckets never parse against a real codex app-server**, which makes the gauge show a false red/blocked state for healthy accounts.

## Root cause

The CLI normalizer (`cli/src/codex/utils/codexUsage.ts`, `normalizeRateLimit` / `parseResetAt`) looks for these keys in the `account/rateLimits/updated` payload:

- window: `window_minutes` / `windowMinutes` / `window` / `minutes`
- reset: `reset_at` / `resetAt` / `resets_in_seconds` / `resets_in_minutes`

But the actual app-server wire payload is (verified with `codex app-server generate-json-schema` on codex 0.145.0, and codex-rs tags 0.120 → 0.147):

```ts
type RateLimitWindow = { usedPercent: number, windowDurationMins: number | null, resetsAt: number | null }
```

`windowDurationMins` / `resetsAt` match nothing, so both the 5h and weekly buckets are **silently dropped on every real codex version**.

## User-visible impact

With both windows gone, the web adapter (`codexBudgetAdapter.ts`) sees `noTimeWindows = true`. A Pro account with healthy subscription windows normally reports `credits: { hasCredits: true, unlimited: false, balance: "0.0000000000" }` (zero top-up credits is normal while the subscription is active), which `isCodexUsageBlocked()` then misreads as exhausted:

```json
{ "rateLimits": {
    "primary":   { "usedPercent": 0, "windowDurationMins": 300,   "resetsAt": 1774278000 },
    "secondary": { "usedPercent": 0, "windowDurationMins": 10080, "resetsAt": 1774278000 },
    "credits":   { "hasCredits": true, "unlimited": false, "balance": "0.0000000000" },
    "planType": "pro", "limitId": "codex", "rateLimitReachedType": null
} } }
```

→ `normalizeCodexUsage` returns `rateLimits: {}` → gauge shows **"Blocked: subscription window and credits both exhausted"**, Credits `0` critical, red 100% ring — while the account actually has 100% quota remaining.

(For context: the original #537 author and this PR's tests both used invented shapes like `{ usedPercent: 12, windowMinutes: 300 }`, which is why this never surfaced.)

## Fix

Tiny — add the real field names to the key lists in `codexUsage.ts` (internal normalized shape unchanged):

```diff
- const direct = record.reset_at ?? record.resetAt;
+ const direct = record.resets_at ?? record.resetsAt ?? record.reset_at ?? record.resetAt;
- const windowMinutes = firstNumber(record, ['window_minutes', 'windowMinutes', 'window', 'minutes']);
+ const windowMinutes = firstNumber(record, ['window_duration_mins', 'windowDurationMins', 'window_minutes', 'windowMinutes', 'window', 'minutes']);
```

(`resetsAt` is unix seconds; the existing `< 10^10 → *1000` handling already covers it.)

A ready implementation with a regression test (real wire shape) and the end-to-end verification lives in https://github.com/swear01/hapi/pull/4 — happy to also open a PR directly against this branch if that's easier for you to cherry-pick.

If two active sessions or pending requests in the same namespace share that prefix, tapping Allow/Deny can approve the wrong permission. This new WeCom path is not bound by Telegram's short callback-data limit, so use exact IDs in the button key and exact lookups. Evidence `hub/src/wecom/sessionView.ts:66`.

The page stays stuck on "No sessions pinned" even when active sessions exist. Evidence `web/src/components/GridView.tsx:58`, `web/src/hooks/queries/useSessions.ts:20`.
  Suggested fix:
  ```ts
  const initializedPinnedRef = useRef(false)

  useEffect(() => {
      if (initializedPinnedRef.current || sessions.length === 0) return
      initializedPinnedRef.current = true

Once that happens, `removeSession` / `closeCell` remove by ID and drop every duplicate cell at once.   const replaceCandidates = sessions.filter((s) =>

One issue: **pending session title events can overwrite the active session title.**

`findSessionFiles()` still scans `pendingSessions` during Claude session rollover. `parseSessionFile()` now forwards every `custom-title` it sees via `onTitleChange`, so a late rename written to the *previous* JSONL file can replace `metadata.name` for the *new* active Claude session.
